segment.source: Mailcatcher
Review the mails captured instead of being sent, and check them for the usual configuration mistakes.
Captured outgoing mails and mail configuration checks
Mailcatcher is active — no mail is being sent
Mailcatcher is active — no mail is being sent. Every mail only lands in the Mailcatcher module.
Mailcatcher is switched on but is not taking effect — mails are still being sent. Do not test with real addresses; please inform your administrator.
Mailcatcher not taking effect — mails are being sent
Mailcatcher
Active — no mail is sent
All outgoing mails are written to files below var/mailcatcher/ instead of being delivered. Switch the catcher off in the Mailcatcher backend module to resume normal mail delivery.
Inactive — mails are delivered normally
Mails are handed to the configured mail transport as usual.
Switched on but ineffective — mails are being sent

The catcher is switched on, but the mail transport still points at regular delivery. The block that assigns FileTransport is missing from config/system/additional.php — see the Installation section of the extension README for the exact lines. Until it is there, the backend cannot capture a single mail.
Switched off, but the transport points at the catcher

The catcher is switched off, yet FileTransport is the configured mail transport, so no mail is delivered. This usually means the assignment was made without the MailcatcherState::isActive() guard around it, or was left behind in settings.php after a debugging session.
Switched on, but locked in this environment

The state file says the catcher is on, but MAILCATCHER_ALLOWED is not 1 and the context is a Production one, so it stays locked and every mail is delivered. Either set MAILCATCHER_ALLOWED=1 in the .env loaded for this context, or switch the catcher off so its state stops claiming otherwise.
The mail is sent as %1$s, but this site sends as %2$s. Mail servers reject that (SPF/DMARC), so the mail is filed as spam or silently dropped.
Use your own address as the sender and put the visitor's address into the reply address instead.
No reply address is set.
Set the reply address to whoever should receive the answer, usually the visitor who filled in the form.
The mail contains an unresolved TYPO3 link (t3://). The recipient sees the raw reference instead of a working link.
Render links in mail templates with f:link.typolink or the absolute URL, so they are resolved before sending.
A placeholder survived rendering and is visible in the mail.
Check the mail template for a typo in the placeholder, or for a variable that was never passed to it.
The mail has an HTML part but no plain text part.
Add a plain text version. It noticeably improves the spam rating and is what some clients display.
The mail has no subject.
Set a subject in the finisher or the mail template.
Sender and recipient are the same address.
Usually a finisher whose sender and recipient fields were filled with the same value — worth a look.
The mail contains a relative link.
A mail program has no base address, so relative links do not work. Always use absolute URLs in mails.
The mail contains an http:// link.
Use https://. Many mail clients flag or rewrite plain http links.
The decoded mail contains replacement characters, which means umlauts or special characters are broken.
The mail was assembled with the wrong character set. Check the template and the data source for their encoding.
Switched on since %1$s
Send
The mail was sent to its original recipients.
Cancel
Delete all captured mails?
This permanently deletes %1$s mails. Mails that were captured instead of delivered are gone for good — nobody ever received them, and there is no second copy.
Yes, delete all
This is a Production system. What is captured here may be real customer communication.
The transport switch in config/system/additional.php is missing or outdated.

Normal requests are captured through the extension’s own ext_localconf.php, so most mail is safe. But reduced bootstraps skip extension configuration — the install tool’s mail test under Environment builds its container without it and would deliver its mail for real. A block that only sets the transport is outdated: with MAIL.dsn or a spool configured, the mail is sent anyway. See the Installation section of the extension README for the current block.
MAILCATCHER_ALLOWED=1 is set in the Production context.

The catcher can be switched on in this context and then stops all outgoing mail. On a staging system that is usually intended; on the live system the variable belongs removed. Development contexts do not need it at all — the catcher is unlocked there anyway.
MAILCATCHER_ALLOWED is set to a value other than 1 and is therefore ignored.
Only the exact value 1 unlocks the catcher. Spellings such as true, yes or on have no effect — remove the variable, or set it to 1.
MAILCATCHER_API_TOKEN is set in the Production context.
The test API is meant for end-to-end tests, not for a live system. Leave the variable empty there; the route then answers 404 and stays closed.
MAILCATCHER_API_TOKEN is shorter than 32 characters.
A short token can be guessed, and the API hands out the full content of every captured mail. Generate a new one with: openssl rand -hex 32 — this is not checked in development contexts.
The requested mail no longer exists.
The mail could not be deleted.
The mail catcher must not be switched on in this environment.
Mail catcher switched on — no mail is being sent from now on.
Mail catcher switched off — mails are being delivered normally again.
Deleted %1$s captured mails.
Active — no mail is being sent
Inactive — mails are delivered normally
Switched on but ineffective — mails are being sent
The transport assignment is missing from config/system/additional.php. Until it is added, switching the catcher on has no effect — see the Reports module for details.
Switched off, but the transport points at the catcher
The mail transport is set to the catcher although it is switched off, so no mail is delivered. Most likely a fixed assignment in the configuration — see the Reports module for details.
Switched on, but locked in this environment — mails are being sent
The switch is on, but the catcher must not run in this context, so nothing is captured and every mail is delivered normally. See the Reports module for how to unlock it.
Locked in this environment. Set MAILCATCHER_ALLOWED=1 to unlock it.
